title: Retry notices must link to the failed run attempt, not the run's latest attempt
answers: retry notice links point to the wrong attempt
rerun failed jobs notice link goes to latest attempt instead of the failed one
how do I link a GitHub Actions run attempt in retry.sh notices
dry-run rerun URL missing attempts segment
body:
Symptom: The "Rerun failed jobs" notice (and dry-run output) links to the run's latest attempt, which may not be the failed attempt that triggered the retry.
Root cause: .github/workflows/retry.sh:rerun built the URL from the run id only (actions/runs/$1), so the attempt number from the runs JSON was dropped.
Fix pattern: Select .attempt in the jq TSV row (`[.id, .workflow, .attempt]`), read it as a third variable in the `while IFS=$'\t' read` loop, pass it through every rerun call (including the deferred protect.yml call), and append `/attempts/$3` to both the dry-run line and the ::notice line.
Constraints: Any new column added to the jq TSV must be matched by an extra variable in the read loop and passed positionally to rerun(); a mismatch silently shifts fields. The protect.yml row is handled separately after `wait`, so it must carry its attempt in protect_attempt too.
applies: Applies to .github/workflows/retry.sh rerun handling and the notices it prints; does not cover how gh run rerun selects which attempt to rerun.
says: The rerun failed jobs notice links to the latest run instead of the failed attempt

search: Rerun handling and notices in .github/workflows/retry.sh must link to the specific failed attempt by selecting .attempt in the jq TSV and appending /attempts/$3 to dry-run and ::notice URLs. The attempt variable must be passed through every rerun call, including protect_attempt for the deferred protect.yml run. Any new column added to the jq TSV must have a corresponding variable in the while read loop to avoid silent field shifting. This guidance applies to notices and rerun handling in .github/workflows/retry.sh, without covering how gh run rerun selects which attempt to rerun.
